text:
michael: seeing a spike in inference tail latency from eastus2-gpu farm since ~20:40 UTC, p99 went from ~120ms -> ~650ms, error rate ticks up. alerts show packet drops on some hosts. anyone else?
sophie: yup, noticed similar on model-serving v2.1 canary — requests time out between pods on same node (east-west).
raj: throws up: `netperf` tests gave small packet loss intermittently, could be host-level shaping? recent maintenance pushed a qos tweak last night.
michael: I see a diff in the host-apply job: added a `tc` root qdisc to enp1s0 for egress policing to cap noisy tenants. commit: `infra/egress-safety 9a3b`
infra-bot: deploy job infra/egress-safety applied to 36 hosts in eastus2 at 2026-03-17T20:05:12Z (run id: 4432)
jamie: can someone run `tc -s qdisc show dev enp1s0` on one of the impacted machines?
olga: ran on gpu-node-42-eastus2:
```
qdisc tbf 8000: root refcnt 2 rate 2Gbit burst 16000b latency 50ms
 Sent 1.2GiB bytes 1.0M pkts
 dropped 412 tx_errors 0

tl: fq_codel 0: dev enp1s0
 Sent 300MiB bytes 240k pkts
 backlog 0b requeues 0
```
michael: weird — both tbf and fq_codel present. tbf on top could be causing microbursts to get dropped, RDMA/GPUDirect flows are sensitive. MTU unchanged though.
raj: checking dmesg on same host — I see `tcp: small buffer squeeze` and `NETDEV WATCHDOG: enp1s0 (kernel): transmit queue 0 timed out` earlier around 20:38
sophie: packet captures from kube-proxy show retransmits and occasional ICMP fragmentation-needed from ovn0 overlay on host. might be shaping interfering with overlay encapsulation.
jamie: quick mitigation: remove the tbf root qdisc on a canary host and observe. command: `sudo tc qdisc del dev enp1s0 root`
michael: did that on gpu-node-42-eastus2 — service p99 dropped back to ~140ms within 30s. no more packet drops on `tc -s`
raj: confirm: after delete, `tc -s qdisc show dev enp1s0` now shows only fq_codel and drops=0.
olga: rolling patch: revert infra/egress-safety for eastus2 hosts, will limit to frontend-only hosts instead.
infra-bot: rollback requested: infra/egress-safety revert queued for eastus2 (batch 36) by olga
sophie: file an incident? prob impact on model SLOs and we'll want a postmortem and safer rollout plan.
michael: yes — short incident doc, postmortem action items: (1) add e2e intra-node perf test to infra change pipeline, (2) baseline RDMA/overlay tests before qos changes, (3) change the tc recipe to avoid root tbf on GPU host NICs, use per-tenant traffic classes scoped to frontend ports only, (4) add alert for host tx drops > 0.1% for 5m.
jamie: I'll own the tc recipe change, raj + olga to run canary, sophie to own alert/dashboard.
olga: rolling revert now; will update when batch completes. :white_check_mark:
michael: thanks all — keeping this thread for the postmortem notes and links. for reference, packet counters and `tc -s` outputs archived at https://internal.redwood/infracluster/1876543210/trace
